gloss: temple gate, main gate of a Buddhist temple

definitions.gloss: temple gate, main gate of a Buddhist temple
definitions.explanation: The main entrance gate of a Buddhist temple complex. Originally referred to the gate of a mountain temple, since many temples were built on mountains. By extension, can also refer to the temple itself.

examples.english: To pass through the temple gate.

examples.japanese: ⟦{立派|りっぱ}→立派：01093_rippa⟧な{山門|さんもん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}えて→見える：01165_mieru⟧きた。
examples.english: An impressive temple gate came into view.

examples.japanese: {南禅寺|なんぜんじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{山門|さんもん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{有数|ゆうすう}→有数：13006_yuusuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{大|おお}きさ→大きさ：10969_ookisa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{誇|ほこ}る→誇る：14180_hokoru⟧。
examples.english: The temple gate of Nanzen-ji boasts one of the largest sizes in Japan.

notes:
{山門|さんもん} literally means "mountain gate" because Buddhist temples in Japan were traditionally built on mountains ({山寺|やまでら}).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {山門|さんもん}: main gate of a Buddhist temple
- ⟦{鳥居|とりい}→鳥居：05956_torii⟧: gate of a Shinto shrine
- ⟦{門|もん}→門：14603_mon⟧: gate (general)

USAGE:
Also written {三門|さんもん} (three gates), referring to the three gates of enlightenment in Buddhism: ⟦{空|くう}→空〜：03949_kuu⟧ (emptiness), {無相|むそう} (formlessness), and {無願|むがん} (desirelessness). Both kanji spellings are used.
